newsitem.title: GERMANY: German watchdog issues warning on aviation insurer.
newsitem.headline: German watchdog issues warning on aviation insurer.

text.p: The German insurance supervisory authority on Monday warned owners of private aircraft against signing new or renewing existing comprehensive coverage offered by the insurer New England International Surety Inc. (NEIS).

"Our extensive investigation found the insurer apparently based in Panama and registered, but not authorised to sell, in Switzerland," Bundesaufsichtsamt fur das Versicherungswesen (BAV) spokeswoman Elke Washausen-Richter told Reuters.
"We have serious doubts as to whether NEIS is, in fact, even a correctly licenced insurance company."
A Hamburg-based broker sells NEIS policies via a further broker based in London, but the insurer is not authorised to offer direct insurance in Germany.

The BAV was unwilling to name either of the involved brokers. "We have firmly asked this Hamburg brokerage company to discontinue dealing with any further contracts for NEIS," Ms Washausen-Richter said.

The BAV investigation determined that the Hamburg broker negotiated more than 700 comprehensive coverage policies for small and mid-sized private planes. In addition, it runs the entire policy administration, including premium collection and claims handling.
"Although we have no evidence that the insurer will not pay in the case of a claim, the latent danger is there," the BAV spokeswoman said.
